title: Postgres
explorerSubtitle: Run procedures, functions, and queries generated by Generate Service for PostgreSQL.
personasSubtitle: CRUD built on gsSpGetPersonas, gsSpInsertPersona, gsSpUpdatePersona, and gsSpDeletePersona.
emptyRequest: This endpoint does not require a request body.
executeToSeeResponse: Run the endpoint to see the response.

operationDescriptions.default: This case demonstrates how Generate Service publishes a PostgreSQL operation as a REST endpoint while respecting the database signature.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a procedure with input and composite output, allowing a client to retrieve one persona by id as a REST object.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can transform a PostgreSQL composite array into a REST list of business objects.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive a composite object from REST, run an insert in PostgreSQL, and return the id generated by the database.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive a collection of composite objects, process a bulk insert in PostgreSQL, and return the inserted count.
operationDescriptions.gsSpUpdatePersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish an update based on a composite object and return a clear result indicator to the consumer.
operationDescriptions.gsSpDeletePersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a parameterized delete operation and tell the consumer whether the operation had an effect.
operationDescriptions.gsSpSavePersonaJsonbInout: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can handle natural JSONB as an INOUT parameter, inserting or updating data and returning the final JSON unescaped in REST.
operationDescriptions.gsSpResumenPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish aggregate calculations defined in PL/pgSQL and return multiple output values in one structured REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonaDetalle: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a composite object with related data, returning a persona with address and children in a single REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonasDetalle: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can return collections of nested composite objects, publishing PostgreSQL hierarchical structures as REST lists.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonasCursorOut: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can consume a procedure with an output REFCURSOR and deliver it to the client as a filtered row list.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonasCursorInout: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can work with an INOUT REFCURSOR, receiving input data and returning a filtered cursor as a REST list.
operationDescriptions.gsSpResumenPersonasOut: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can map multiple OUT parameters, combining numeric totals and boolean flags in a single REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertarPersonasCursor: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive a cursor with business records, process them in PostgreSQL, and return the total rows handled.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonasEstadoCursor: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a procedure with multiple output cursors, separating active and inactive results in the REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonaJson: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can return native PostgreSQL JSON as natural REST JSON, without turning it into escaped text.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersonaJson: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive natural JSON from REST, let PostgreSQL extract its properties, and return the generated id.
operationDescriptions.gsSpUpdatePersonaJson: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can update records using natural JSON as a flexible input contract and return the operation result.
operationDescriptions.gsSpSavePersonaJsonInout: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can handle natural JSON as an INOUT parameter, resolving insert or update and returning the resulting document.
operationDescriptions.gsSpGetPersonaJsonb: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose PostgreSQL JSONB as natural REST JSON, preserving a response that web clients can consume directly.
operationDescriptions.gsSpInsertPersonaJsonb: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive natural JSONB from REST, insert it through PL/pgSQL logic, and return the created identifier.
operationDescriptions.gsSpUpdatePersonaJsonb: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can update data using natural JSONB input and return a boolean confirmation to the consumer.
operationDescriptions.gsSpIncrementarEdad: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose scalar INOUT parameters, sending an initial value and returning the value modified by PostgreSQL.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasTable: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish a RETURNS TABLE function as a REST endpoint, delivering typed rows filtered by state.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasSetof: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can transform a RETURNS SETOF function into a REST list of PostgreSQL records.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonaRow: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a function that returns a table row and convert it into a REST object.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonaObj: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish a function returning a PostgreSQL composite type as a REST response object.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasNombresSetof: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can return scalar SETOF results as a simple list consumable from REST.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasJsonSetof: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose SETOF JSON as a list of natural JSON documents, without escaped strings.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasJsonbSetof: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose SETOF JSONB as a REST list of natural JSON documents.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonaJsonObj: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can combine composite types and JSONB fields, delivering structured data with flexible JSON content.
operationDescriptions.gsFnSavePersonaJsonObj: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive a composite type with JSONB data, run an insert or update, and return the process result.
operationDescriptions.gsFnResumenPersonas: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish a function with OUT parameters and return an aggregate summary as a REST response.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasPorEstado: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose functions with filters and default values defined in PostgreSQL, publishing them as a REST contract.
operationDescriptions.gsFnBuscarPersona: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish an identifier-based lookup function and return the matched row as a REST object.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonasPorIds: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can receive PostgreSQL arrays from REST as lists and use them to return related records.
operationDescriptions.gsFnGetPersonaNullable: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can represent nullable columns in a REST response, preserving NULL values defined by the function.
operationDescriptions.gsFnTouchPersonaVoid: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a RETURNS VOID function to run an action without output data and answer with a REST confirmation.
operationDescriptions.gsFnInsertPersonaThenError: This case demonstrates that Generate Service handles transactionality when a function inserts data and then fails, rolling back the operation and propagating the error to the consumer.
operationDescriptions.gsFnErrorControlado: This case demonstrates that Generate Service correctly propagates a controlled PL/pgSQL exception, allowing database business rules to be reflected in the API.
operationDescriptions.gsFnIncrementarEdadInout: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a function with a scalar INOUT parameter, receiving a value and returning the modified result.
operationDescriptions.gsFnResumenInout: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can map multiple INOUT parameters and return the values recalculated by the PostgreSQL function.
operationDescriptions.gsFnResumenMixto: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can combine INOUT and OUT parameters in the same function, generating a coherent REST input and output contract.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonaById: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can publish a parameterized SQL query as a REST endpoint, allowing a client to retrieve one persona by id without creating a function or procedure.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasByNombre: This case demonstrates flexible text search with ILIKE. The client sends part of a name and Generate Service returns the matching typed rows.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasByActivo: This case demonstrates a direct boolean filter. The client can request active or inactive personas and receive a REST list with selected columns.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasSelfJoinActivo: This case demonstrates that a self-join query is also generated as a REST endpoint, useful for comparing rows in the same table under a shared rule.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasActivasWith: This case demonstrates that Generate Service can expose a WITH/CTE query, separating filter logic and returning the result as a business list.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasTotalHijosWith: This case demonstrates a query with CTE, LEFT JOIN, and aggregation. The client sees personas filtered by state together with the child count calculated by PostgreSQL.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasStatsWith: This case demonstrates an aggregate WITH query that returns REST-ready metrics: total, average, minimum age, and maximum age.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasByCityJoin: This case demonstrates a JOIN query between persona and address. The client filters by city and receives combined data without assembling joins outside the API.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasByJson: This case demonstrates that Generate Service accepts a natural JSON array in REST, passes it to PostgreSQL as raw JSON, and returns personas related to the ids in the document.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasByJsonb: This case demonstrates the same flow with JSONB: the client sends a natural JSON array, PostgreSQL processes it as jsonb, and the API returns typed rows.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasAsJson: This case demonstrates that a query can build native JSON in PostgreSQL and Generate Service returns it as natural REST JSON, not escaped text.
operationDescriptions.gsQPersonasAsJsonb: This case demonstrates that a query can aggregate results as JSONB and publish them in REST as a natural JSON document ready for web clients.
operationDescriptions.gsQInsertPersona: This case demonstrates an INSERT query without RETURNING. Generate Service exposes it as POST and returns boolean when it executes without exception.
operationDescriptions.gsQInsertPersonaSelect: This case demonstrates an INSERT based on SELECT. The client sends variable data and PostgreSQL completes the new record from a base persona; the REST response is boolean when there is no exception.
operationDescriptions.gsQUpdatePersona: This case demonstrates a parameterized UPDATE query. Generate Service publishes the update as a REST endpoint and returns an execution boolean when there is no exception.
operationDescriptions.gsQDeletePersona: This case demonstrates a parameterized DELETE query. The client sends the identifier and Generate Service returns boolean when the delete executes without error.

support.title: Postgres Support
support.subtitle: Guide to procedures, functions, SQL queries, composite types, arrays, cursors, and JSON/JSONB published by Generate Service for PostgreSQL.
support.jsonSubtitle: PostgreSQL 17 documents JSON and JSONB as native types. JSON preserves the input text; JSONB stores a decomposed binary representation and is usually better for processing and indexes.
support.jsonRawNote: Generate Service maps JSON and JSONB to String in Java, but DTOs use @RawJson on input and @JsonRawValue on output. The UI must therefore send and receive natural JSON objects or arrays, not strings containing escaped JSON.
support.capabilitiesSubtitle: The Postgres catalog covers procedures with IN/OUT/INOUT, RETURNS TABLE functions, RETURNS SETOF functions, SQL queries, composite types, arrays, REFCURSOR, and native JSON/JSONB.
support.typeMappingTitle: Postgres types supported by Generate Service
support.typeMappingSubtitle: Scoped equivalence table between PostgreSQL types used or confirmed for this suite and the generated Java/REST contract.
support.typeMappingNote: This table does not document every existing PostgreSQL type. PostgreSQL types outside this scope remain pending until support is confirmed in the generated contract.
support.rulesSubtitle: These rules apply to the generated microservice and keep the customer-facing contract stable.

nativeJson.title: Native types
nativeJson.description: PostgreSQL uses JSON and JSONB directly in procedures, functions, and composite types; no custom alias is needed for this case.

jsonOperators.title: Reading inside PL/pgSQL
jsonOperators.description: The suite procedures read fields with ->> and cast to INTEGER, DATE, or BOOLEAN when needed.

javaRaw.title: Java keeps raw String
javaRaw.description: The Java contract keeps String internally, but raw annotations serialize and deserialize real JSON.

naturalRest.title: Natural REST payload
naturalRest.description: The request must send normal JSON objects or arrays; Generate Service converts that raw value into the internal String.

procedures.title: Procedures
procedures.description: Supports PL/pgSQL procedures with IN, OUT, and INOUT, including scalar, composite, array, and JSON/JSONB responses.

functions.title: Functions
functions.description: Exposes functions returning scalars, rows, composite types, VOID, and OUT parameters as POST endpoints.

setReturningFunctions.title: SETOF/TABLE functions
setReturningFunctions.description: RETURNS SETOF and RETURNS TABLE are published as lists in the response DTO.

queries.title: SQL queries
queries.description: Free SQL queries are published as POST endpoints, including filters, JOIN, WITH/CTE, aggregates, and natural JSON/JSONB.

compositeTypes.title: Composite types
compositeTypes.description: CREATE TYPE generates Java models annotated as OBJECT, for example GsPersonaObj and GsPersonaDetalleObj.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.description: Parameters such as gs_persona_obj[] and INTEGER[] are represented in REST as arrays/lists.

refcursors.title: REFCURSOR
refcursors.description: OUT or INOUT cursors are materialized as row lists according to the generated DTO.

jsonTypes.title: JSON/JSONB
jsonTypes.description: JSON and JSONB are treated as dynamic JSON in REST through @RawJson and @JsonRawValue.

transactions.title: Transactional tests
transactions.description: VOID and controlled-error functions validate rollback and exception handling.

rules.snakeCase: In PostgreSQL, snake_case is recommended for parameters, SQL aliases, and PL/pgSQL names.
rules.camelCase: Generate Service transforms PostgreSQL names to camelCase for Java and REST contracts.
rules.endpointNames: PL/pgSQL names and queries become generated method names and REST endpoint names.
rules.envOverride: The per-engine base URL is configured from .env with API_ENDPOINT_POSTGRES; when it is not set, the UI falls back to http://localhost:8083. Backend REST endpoint paths can also be changed with environment variables.
rules.jsonProperty: Variable names exposed in JSON can be adjusted with the Jackson @JsonProperty annotation.

rules.postOnly: All generated Postgres endpoints in this project use POST.
rules.apiBase: The generated controller uses /api as its base path, so the final route is /api/{operation}.
rules.envOverride: REST routes can be changed with API_REST_ENDPOINT_* variables in the generated backend.
rules.serverSideFetch: The UI executes endpoints through server actions.

rules.nativeTypes: JSON and JSONB are native PostgreSQL 17 types.
rules.dynamicContract: Generate Service keeps them as internal String values, not rigid DTOs.
rules.naturalPayload: REST sends natural JSON: an object or array, not escaped JSON text.
rules.jsonbNote: JSONB can reorder keys and normalize semantically insignificant details; JSON preserves the input text.
rules.compositeJson: In gs_persona_json_obj, the datos field is JSONB and is exposed as natural JSON.

rules.officialVersion: This guide uses PostgreSQL 17 as the official reference, matching the postgres:17 image in docker-compose.
rules.outOfScope: Official types without confirmed mapping stay out of scope in this documentation.

rules.repositoryIntegrity: After the microservice is generated, Generate Service validates the integrity of generated repositories.
rules.licenseValidation: The generated API includes local integrity and license validations through a secure token issued by Generate Service. These validations run inside the generated API itself and do not require calls to external licensing services.
rules.signedMetadata: Do not modify @Callable, @SpParameter, types, inputs, outputs, PL/pgSQL names, or signed queries.
rules.regenerateOnSourceChange: If the data source, procedure, function, query, parameters, or types change, the microservice must be regenerated.
rules.oneEndpointPerSource: Each PL/pgSQL unit or query the customer wants to consume should be generated as its own stable API source.

rules.controllers: Controllers can add validation, input adaptation, or response enrichment.
rules.services: Services can add business logic before or after invoking the generated source.
rules.businessLogic: Responses can be recalculated, composed, or transformed without changing signed metadata.
rules.sourceLock: The generated data source is protected: repositories, signatures, parameters, query definitions, and PL/pgSQL definitions are not manually changed.
